# `•plot` — Plots

`X •plot Y` returns a plot spec: a keyed vector holding the data `Y` and
the settings `X`. Its [renderer](xml.ipynb#rich-display) displays the
spec as an SVG chart. Plain text on the left is shorthand for the `mark`
setting. [Plots](plot.ipynb) shows each mark and setting with examples.

The series and axes depend on the structure of `Y`:

- A vector’s values are plotted against `0…n-1`.
- The keys of a keyed vector of numbers are the x labels.
- Each row of a matrix is plotted as a series. Row keys name the series.
  Column keys label x.
- With the `cell` mark, each row of a matrix is a row of cells, coloured
  by value. Row keys label the rows, and row 0 is at the top.
- Each column of a table, a keyed vector of equal-length columns, is
  plotted as a series. A column named `x` supplies the x values.
- A vector or matrix of plots is drawn as a figure.

`color` also takes one number per point. `palette` turns these numbers
into colours, over the range of every series in the plot. A cell is
coloured by its value unless `color` is set.

A direct [`•mime`](system/mime.qmd) call on a spec reports these errors:
`DOMAIN` for unknown settings or values, and for cells mixed with other
marks; `LENGTH` when series, colours, sizes or labels don’t match the x
values; `RANK` for data that isn’t a vector, matrix or table.

## Data

`•plot` draws one series for each row of a matrix. Its column keys label
the x axis. With `"legend":"end"`, each line is labelled with its name
beside its last point:

``` bpl
sales←["city":"NY" "LA";"month":"Jan" "Feb" "Mar"]:[10 20 30◇40 50 60]
["legend":"end"] •plot sales
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-3-output-1.svg)

For a keyed vector of numbers, `•plot` uses the keys as x labels:

``` bpl
•plot ["Jan":10 "Feb":20 "Mar":15]
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-4-output-1.svg)

In a table, a column named `x` supplies the x values. Every other column
is a series:

``` bpl
["mark":"point"] •plot ["x":150 160 170 180;"weight":50 62 68 80]
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-5-output-1.svg)

## Settings

`•plot` returns the plot spec, an ordinary keyed vector. Pass settings
as the left argument of `•plot`, or assign them to the spec afterwards.
Assigning through a dot path creates any missing settings along that
path. Setting `legend.position` to a corner draws a boxed legend, titled
with the name of the row axis:

``` bpl
p←["mark":"bar" "title":"Sales"] •plot sales
p.legend.position←"top-left"
p
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-6-output-1.svg)

A `"log"` scale suits values that grow by factors:

``` bpl
q←•plot 1 10 100 1000
q.y.scale←"log"
q
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-7-output-1.svg)

`ticks` is a number of ticks, a vector of positions, or a keyed vector
from labels to positions:

``` bpl
r←•plot 3 1 4 1 5
r.x.ticks←["first":0 "last":4]
r.y.ticks←3
r
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-8-output-1.svg)

## Series styles

`mark`, `color`, `size` and `labels` style every series. To style one
series, put these fields under its name in `series`.

- `color` is `"#rrggbb"` or a colour name: `"blue"`, `"orange"`,
  `"green"`, `"red"`, `"purple"`, `"brown"`, `"pink"`, `"gray"`,
  `"olive"`, `"cyan"`, `"black"` or `"white"`. Series without a `color`
  are given the colours from `"blue"` to `"cyan"` in order. Give `color`
  one colour or one number per point to colour each point separately, as
  [Colour from data](#colour-from-data) describes.
- `size` is the point radius or line width in pixels. For points, pass
  one number per point to `size` to set each point’s size by value.
- `labels` is `1` to label each point with its value, or one label per
  point. Use `""` to leave a point unlabelled. Overlapping labels are
  moved apart.

`•plot` does no curve fitting. Here the trend line is a least-squares
fit computed in BPL and drawn as a second series:

``` bpl
x←1 2 3 4 5 6 ◇ y←2.1 3.9 6.2 7.8 10.1 12.2
m←x*⊗0 1
fitted←["mark":"point"] •plot ["x":x "sales":y "trend":m+.×y⌹m]
fitted.series.trend.mark←"line"
fitted.series.sales.labels←1
fitted.legend.position←"bottom-right"
fitted
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-9-output-1.svg)

## Colour from data

Pass one number per point in `color` to colour each point by value.
`palette` maps the numbers onto colours, from the lowest value in the
plot to the highest. `palette` is `"viridis"` (the default), `"gray"`,
or a list of colours spaced evenly along that range. With
`"colorbar":$t`, the scale is shown beside the plot:

``` bpl
["mark":"point";"size":8;"color":30 25 40 35;"colorbar":$t] •plot ["x":150 160 170 180;"weight":50 62 68 80]
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-10-output-1.svg)

The `cell` mark draws each row of a matrix as a row of cells, coloured
by value. Row 0 is at the top, matching the printed matrix. Row keys
label the rows:

``` bpl
["mark":"cell" "colorbar":$t] •plot sales
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-11-output-1.svg)

A Sierpinski carpet is a 3×3 block with its centre removed. Each filled
cell holds a smaller copy of the whole carpet. `kron` is the Kronecker
product: each item of
[`α`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/alpha.html) scales a
copy of [`ω`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/omega.html).
`block↣kron⍣3 block` applies `kron` three times, giving an 81×81 carpet.
Setting `"axes":$f` leaves only the cells, without axes or ticks.
`p.y.axis←$f` hides only the y axis. An `axis` setting in `x` or `y`
takes precedence over `axes` for that axis. Because `•plot` draws each
run of same-coloured cells in a row as one rectangle, the picture has
far fewer SVG elements than cells:

``` bpl
block←[1 1 1
       1 0 1
       1 1 1]
kron←{α×⍥ρω ρ 0 2 1 3⍉α×⊗ω}
plotopts←["mark":"cell";"palette":"white" "black";"axes":$f;"width":400;"height":400]
plotopts •plot block↣kron⍣3 block
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-12-output-1.svg)

## Figures

Pass a vector or matrix of plots to `•plot` to display them as a figure.
A vector is one row, and
[`⍪`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/comma-bar.html) makes
a column. Repeat a plot in adjacent cells to make it span them. `widths`
and `heights` give relative cell sizes. With `"share":1`, plots in the
same column share one x range, and plots in the same row share one y
range:

``` bpl
["title":"Overview" "height":500] •plot [p p◇fitted •plot[3 1 4 1 5]]
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-13-output-1.svg)

The following example combines these figure settings to make a scatter
plot with marginal histograms. Evaluating a normal distribution’s
`quantile` at evenly spread probabilities gives normally distributed
values without randomness:

``` bpl
n←•distribution "normal"
x←n.quantile 1|0.5+0.618034×ι400
y←0.6×x + 0.8×n.quantile 1|0.5+0.754878×ι400
```

`•plot` does no binning. `count` counts the values within 0.25 of each
bin centre. Each histogram is a bar chart of counts. `flip` turns the
second one on its side:

``` bpl
centers←¯2.75+0.5×ι12
count←{+/ ω≥α-0.25 ∧ ω<α+0.25}
hist←{["x":centers "count":centers⁝count¨⊂ω]}
top←["mark":"bar"] •plot hist x
side←["mark":"bar" "flip":1] •plot hist y
```

With `heights` of `1 4`, the top histogram is a fifth of the figure’s
height. With `widths` of `4 1`, the side histogram is a fifth of the
figure’s width. The top-right corner is empty because its position holds
[`⍬`](https://answerdotai.github.io/basedpl/glyphs/zilde.html). With
`share`, the top histogram shares the scatter plot’s x range, and the
side histogram shares its y range:

``` bpl
scatter←["mark":"point" "size":2] •plot ["x":x "y":y]
grid←["widths":4 1;"heights":1 4;"share":1;"width":500;"height":500]
grid •plot [top ⍬◇scatter side]
```

![](plot_files/figure-commonmark/cell-16-output-1.svg)
